text:
I think you need to understand a couple of things here. All these top company CEOs are saying good things about Indiamarket. just because they have to exit their investments at a good valuation. Imagine if they started pointing out the real issues: they would not be able to pull their investments out at a good profit. So, they say good things, and when the time is right, they just start exiting (which is already what FIIs are doing currently).

Now, there are two main things working against investing in India:

1. Rupee depreciation: for an FII, you do not invest in dollars, you invest in rupees. If the rupee is depreciating 5-7% per year, you have to factor that into your actual returns. If you are making an average of 8% long-term, but currency depreciation eats up 7%, your net return can even end up negative. Because of that, it makes very little sense for someone outside India to invest in the Indian market.
2. Long-term capital gains tax: it is currently and that also works directly against returns.

So, I really do not think you should take every public comment optimistically.

The fact is this type of channels invite CEOs of reputed mutual fund companies and they will say keep SIPing reason being every time you make a SIP, you pay an amount to those companies and third party platforms like groww, zerodha etc so that even in the crashing market they can keep earning.

text:
Fact check: investing ₹10k/month for 30 years totals ₹36 lakh, and ₹2k/month with 10% annual step-up totals ~₹40 lakh. By the final year, the 2k SIP grows to ~₹30k/month (inflation-adjusted ~₹5k), while the 10k SIP would be ~₹10k (~₹2k today). After 30 years, a corpus of ₹7–10 crore adjusts for inflation to ~₹1.2–1.5 crore today.

So even though the 2k step-up SIP starts small, it eventually costs much more in later years, and the difference in total investment is only ~₹20 lakh. Also, part of the invested amount loses value over time due to inflation, so the “real” invested ₹40 lakh is less in today’s terms, yet the final corpus is worth ~₹1.5 crore. It’s not huge, but better to have something than nothing. [edit:- i just calculated the total invested amount after inflation and its insane for 10k its 16lac approx and for 2k its 10 lac approx]

After 30 years you have to pay this much ammount every money  

To calculate the SIP amount after 30 years with a 10% step-up every year, we use the formula for compounded annual growth:

Amount in year n = Initial SIP × (1 + Step-up rate)^(n - 1)

Here:

Initial SIP = 2000

Step-up rate = 10% = 0.10

Duration = 30 years

Let's calculate it:

Amount in year 30 = 2000 × (1 + 0.10)^(30 - 1)
= 2000 × (1.10)^29

Calculating:

1.10 raised to the power of 29 is approximately 15.91.

Thus:
Amount in year 30 = 2000 × 15.91 = 31,820 INR.

After 30 years, the SIP amount will be ₹31,820 per month.

Each year, your SIP increases by 10%.
So, SIP in year n = ₹2,000 × (1.10)^(n−1)
SIP amount after 30 years:
SIP in the 30th year = ₹2,000 × (1.10)^(30−1)
= ₹2,000 × (1.10)^29
Now calculate:
(1.10)^29 ≈ 15.86
So,
👉 SIP after 30 years = ₹2,000 × 15.86 ≈ ₹31,720/month

text:
In mutual fund SIPs, investors invest on a fixed date every month. However, the fund house does not allot units based on that day's NAV (Net Asset Value). Instead, it often uses the NAV of the next business day or the day when the markets are open.

Because of this, investors don’t always get the benefit of the exact day they invested and sometimes, it even results in a small loss.

In this video, let's understand why mutual fund houses don’t use the same day’s NAV and why the SIP units are not allotted on the very day your SIP amount is debited.

context: Why is your mutual fund SIP giving negative returns?
text:
Apne audience ko samjhaiye ki SIP ka duration matter karta hai. 
1) nifty 50 index ya large cap 5-6+ years 
2) flexicap 7+ years kyunki thoda S+M cap hota hai, mostly large cap allocation
3) small, mid, multicap etc 10+ years ke liye hota hai.
Covid ke baad wala returns sirf illusion thha. Majaal nhi hai ki long term returns koi fund 20% se jyada de de.

Nifty 50- 12%
Flexicap- 13-14%
Large and midcap 14-15%
Midcap - 15-16%
Small cap 17-18%
Multicap 15-16%
Realistic target rakhiye aur allocation sahi rakhe.
Nifty 50 index plus flexicap 50-60%
Mid and small cap 40-50% 
Jyada risk lene se koi faayda nhi, market crash hone par insaan ko aukaat ka pata chalta hai.
Issliye convenient amount se SIP start kijiye, shuruaat me HDFC BAF se start karna better hai. Yahi portfolio ko sambhalega.

context: Long Time SIP Scam
text:
Here are all the numbers used in this calculation:

Inputs:
	1.	Monthly Investment: ₹10,000
	2.	Investment Duration: 20 years (240 months)
	3.	Inflation Rate: 6% per annum
	4.	Annual Interest Rate (Return): 15% per annum
	5.	Long-Term Capital Gains Tax Rate: 12.5% on gains exceeding ₹1,25,000
	6.	Exemption Limit for LTCG Tax: ₹1,25,000

Results:
	1.	Total Actual Investment (without inflation adjustment): ₹24,00,000
	•	₹10,000 × 240 months.
	2.	Inflation-Adjusted Total Investment: ₹14,13,843
	3.	Future Value of Investment (at 15% annual interest): ₹1,51,59,550
	4.	Capital Gains (Future Value - Actual Investment):
	•	₹1,51,59,550 - ₹24,00,000 = ₹1,27,59,550
	5.	Taxable Capital Gains (Exceeding ₹1,25,000):
	•	₹1,27,59,550 - ₹1,25,000 = ₹1,26,34,550
	6.	LTCG Tax Payable:
	•	₹1,26,34,550 × 12.5% = ₹15,79,319
	7.	Future Value After Tax:
	•	₹1,51,59,550 - ₹15,79,319 = ₹1,35,80,231
	8.	Inflation-Adjusted Future Value After Tax:
	•	₹1,35,80,231 ÷ (1.06^20) = ₹42,34,380

Summary:
	•	Inflation-adjusted total investment: ₹14,13,843
	•	Post-tax, inflation-adjusted future value: ₹42,34,380

your investment effectively tripled in terms of real value (adjusted for inflation) over 20 years:
	•	Inflation-adjusted total investment: ₹14,13,843
	•	Post-tax, inflation-adjusted future value: ₹42,34,380

This indicates that despite inflation and taxes, your investment grew approximately 3 times its original real value over 20 years, thanks to the 15% annual return compounded over time.

Sir, sometimes we worry about which index mutual fund is best or whether it will grow in the future. In such cases, NPS can also be considered. It has Tier I (retirement plan) and Tier II (investment plan like mutual funds), with flexible asset allocation across equity, corporate bonds, and government bonds. For youngsters, allocation can be more towards equity, and for seniors more towards government bonds.

Returns in NPS Tier II and index mutual funds are almost the same as both depend on market conditions, but NPS is more hassle-free.

text:
आपके द्वारा UPI mandate और उसके failure पर charges न लगने संबंधी जो जानकारी अपने वीडियो में दी गई है, वह पूर्ण रूप से स्पष्ट और प्रमाणित नहीं है, जिससे सामान्य उपभोक्ताओं में भ्रम की स्थिति उत्पन्न हो रही है।
UPI प्रणाली (NPCI के दिशानिर्देशों के अनुसार) में सामान्यतः UPI transactions पर कोई अलग charge नहीं लगाया जाता है, लेकिन यह पूर्णतः सभी परिस्थितियों पर लागू हो, ऐसा नहीं है। विभिन्न बैंकों की अपनी policy, transaction type और failure/retry परिस्थितियों के अनुसार charges लागू हो सकते हैं।
अतः केवल एक सामान्य statement देकर यह कहना कि “UPI mandate fail होने पर कोई charge नहीं लगता”, हर मामले में सही नहीं माना जा सकता।
आपसे निवेदन है कि किसी भी वित्तीय विषय पर जानकारी साझा करने से पहले NPCI guidelines एवं संबंधित बैंकों की official policy की पुष्टि अवश्य करें, ताकि जनता को गलत जानकारी न मिले और किसी प्रकार का भ्रम या आर्थिक नुकसान न हो।

text:
राहुल सर, सच में दिल से बोल रहा हूँ—SIP पर इतना क्लियर और जमीन से जुड़ा हुआ वीडियो बहुत कम देखने को मिलता है। आपने जो ‘कमिटमेंट’ वाली बात समझाई [05:48], वही असली चीज है जिसे हम लोग अक्सर नजरअंदाज कर देते हैं। हम जैसे ही मार्केट थोड़ा नीचे जाता है, घबरा जाते हैं और SIP रोक देते हैं, जबकि आपने बहुत सरल तरीके से यह समझा दिया कि असली फायदा तो उसी समय मिलता है जब हम लगातार बने रहते हैं। आपने जो डेटा के साथ यह दिखाया कि लंबे समय तक डिसिप्लिन बनाए रखना ही वेल्थ क्रिएशन की असली चाबी है, वह बात सीधे दिमाग में बैठ गई।
साथ ही ‘महंगाई (Inflation)’ [08:47] को जोड़कर आपने जो लक्ष्य तय करने का तरीका बताया, वह मेरे लिए बिल्कुल नया और आंखें खोलने वाला था, क्योंकि हम अक्सर सिर्फ रिटर्न के बारे में सोचते हैं लेकिन असल में पैसे की वैल्यू समय के साथ कैसे बदलती है, यह समझना उतना ही जरूरी है। और ‘स्टेप-अप SIP’ [13:00] का जो आपने उदाहरण दिया, वह बहुत ही practical लगा—क्योंकि income बढ़ती है तो investment भी बढ़ना चाहिए, यह बात आपने बहुत natural तरीके से समझा दी।
मैं खुद अभी investing सीख रहा हूँ और honestly आपका यह वीडियो देखकर ऐसा लगा कि अब चीजें थोड़ी-थोड़ी clear होने लगी हैं। आपकी सबसे अच्छी बात यह लगी कि आपने कोई भी चीज घुमा-फिराकर नहीं बोली, सब कुछ सीधा और समझने लायक बताया। ऐसे ही knowledge share करते रहिए सर, सच में बहुत value मिलती है। #SIPPart2 का इंतजार रहेगा 🙏
